DNR's approval pursuant to Wisconsin Administration Code NR 154.05 and endorsement of the Notice of Intent supports the conclusion that if the Airport Spur is constructed, the project will not violate the National Ambient Air Quality Standards or significantly degrade air quality. In no case will carbon monoxide levels exceed 75% of the standards nor exceed non-degradation levels taken as 7 ppm for the 1-hour level or 2 ppm for the 8-hour level as a result of nearby vehicular travel adjacent to the sensitive receptor sites. FHWA adoption constitutes determination that the project is consistent with the State Implementation Plan.
The air quality maintenance plan for Southeastern Wisconsin is currently in the process of being developed by the Southeastern Wisconsin Regional Planning Commission (SEWRPC) with the assistance of the Wisconsin Departments of Transportation and Natural Resources. It is anticipated that the plan will be completed by December 1975 with a formal report published by July 1, 1976 which is in accordance with latest EPA regulations. According to the SEWRPC the studies completed to date indicates that the elimination of automotive congestion through highway construction is an effective means of reducing the total emissions of carbon monoxide and hydrocarbons within the region.
Preliminary plans for General Mitchell Field's Comprehensive Master Plan is currently underway. Close coordination between the proposed freeway facility and airport expansion developments will be adhered to.
